text:
Yes—**excoriation disorder (skin-picking disorder)** is usually treated by a therapist or psychologist familiar with **body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs)**, often using **ComB (Comprehensive Behavioral treatment), habit-reversal training, CBT, ACT, and sometimes ERP**. A psychiatrist can evaluate medication options if needed.

### Strong Texas telehealth options

- **Baylor Medicine OCD Program — Houston**  
  Offers **virtual appointments to people living anywhere in Texas**, is accepting new patients, and specifically treats excoriation disorder, trichotillomania, OCD, and related conditions. They treat children and adults and can coordinate psychiatric medication care. Call **713-798-3080**. ([bcm.edu](https://www.bcm.edu/healthcare/specialties/psychiatry-and-behavioral-sciences/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-program/frequently-asked-questions?utm_source=openai))

- **Suzanne Mouton-Odum, PhD — Psychology Houston**  
  A prominent BFRB specialist who treats **skin picking and other BFRBs** with telehealth for Texas residents. She works with children, teens, and adults and lists CBT, ACT, habit-reversal, and ComB-related approaches. Insurance, private-pay, and sliding-scale options are listed. ([bfrb.org](https://www.bfrb.org/medical-therapeutic-providers/suzanne-mouton-odum%2C-ph.d.?utm_source=openai))

- **Julia Bickerstaff, MS, LPC — JB Counseling & Wellness**  
  Provides virtual therapy across Texas, specializing in OCD-related disorders and BFRBs including skin-picking and hair-pulling. Her listed approaches include **CBT, ACT, ERP, and ComB**. Her practice offers a free brief consultation. ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/providers/bickerstaff-julia/?utm_source=openai))

- **Kendra Watkins — Abundant Life Counseling**  
  Offers **100% telehealth in Texas** and specifically treats excoriation and other OCD-related disorders using ERP/CBT-informed care. ([ocdcounseling.org](https://ocdcounseling.org/about/?utm_source=openai))

- **Chris Clark, LMFT**  
  Listed as accepting online clients in Texas and treating skin-picking, OCD, trichotillomania, and hoarding. The listing indicates availability for children through older adults and lists several insurance networks, though you should confirm current availability and coverage. ([zencare.co](https://zencare.co/provider/therapist/chris-clark?utm_source=openai))

- **Aaron H. Fink, MD — Houston**  
  A Texas-licensed psychiatrist offering telehealth who treats compulsive skin-picking across age groups and provides assessment, medication management, and psychotherapy. ([bfrb.org](https://www.bfrb.org/medical-therapeutic-providers/aaron-h.-fink?utm_source=openai))

- **Priscilla Elliott, MA, LPC — Courage Counseling**  
  A long-time BFRB specialist in Austin. She offers an online adult BFRB group via Google Meet for skin-picking, hair-pulling, and nail-biting; an individual screening is required before joining. ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/providers/elliott-priscilla/?utm_source=openai))

### Where I’d start

- **Most comprehensive program:** Baylor OCD Program  
- **Most BFRB-focused individual care:** Suzanne Mouton-Odum or Priscilla Elliott  
- **Private online therapist with statewide telehealth:** Julia Bickerstaff or Kendra Watkins  
- **Medication evaluation or combined treatment:** Baylor or Aaron Fink

When contacting a provider, ask:

> “Do you specifically treat excoriation disorder/dermatillomania, and do you use ComB or habit-reversal training? Are sessions fully telehealth for someone physically located in Texas, and do you accept my insurance?”

If the picking has caused significant wounds, bleeding, scarring, or possible infection, it is also appropriate to involve a primary-care clinician or dermatologist alongside behavioral treatment.
